title: Novobo: Supporting Teachers’ Peer Learning of Instructional Gestures by Teaching a Mentee AI-Agent Together
extended_summary:
This paper addresses how generative AI and teachable-agent designs might support teachers’ professional learning around instructional gestures, a form of embodied pedagogical skill that is difficult to teach through text alone. The authors argue that existing approaches to gesture training are often time-consuming, overly prescriptive, or insufficiently reflective of context, and propose a teacher-facing AI mentee that can stimulate peer learning rather than simply deliver feedback.

The intervention, Novobo, is a generative AI teachable agent built around retrieval-augmented generation and a multi-agent architecture. Teachers pose classroom scenarios, review AI-generated gesture suggestions with literature references, rate and comment on them, demonstrate their own gestures using a skeletal webcam mirror, and then explain the pedagogical rationale for their choices. This design intentionally frames the AI as a novice mentee so that teachers can mentor it together, externalize tacit knowledge, and discuss gesture use in a low-pressure collaborative setting.

The study involved 30 teachers from seven local primary schools, including two special education schools, in collaborative study-group sessions. The evaluation combined vignette analysis of interaction behavior with thematic analysis of focus-group reflections, yielding evidence that the system helped teachers share, compare, and refine embodied knowledge through discussion and demonstration. Teachers also valued cited sources and the mentor-mentee framing, which reduced skepticism and social pressure. The paper concludes that teachable agents can support collaborative professional development for teachers, but the reported evidence is exploratory rather than outcome-comparative, and the system was not evaluated for long-term learning gains or classroom impact.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI GPT-based large language model system used to generate instructional-gesture descriptions, analyze instructional intentions, and support conversational interaction in a teachable-agent workflow.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the underlying LLM family for Novobo’s multi-agent architecture, including gesture generation, intention analysis, and conversation management via GPT-4-turbo and GPT-3.5-turbo.

findings.finding_summary: In a qualitative/mixed-methods field evaluation with 30 teachers across 10 collaborative sessions, Novobo’s GPT-based design supported teachers’ peer learning of instructional gestures. The paper reports that teachers externalized tacit knowledge, exchanged ideas, and co-constructed understanding while interacting with the agent; no quantitative effect size was reported.
findings.measure: Teacher peer-learning processes, knowledge exchange, and responses in field evaluation and focus groups

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical field evaluation with teachers, but it is qualitative/mixed-methods rather than a controlled trial. The evidence is useful for design insight but does not establish causal impact.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports positive interaction and collaborative-learning effects, but no quantitative effect size or causal estimate is provided. Impact is therefore suggestive but unclear in magnitude.
